bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses the BPS label to frame PRT as an intervention that implements the model in practice. It describes pain as influenced by biological, psychological, and social factors but does not operationalize the model into specific variables or mechanisms across all three domains. The social domain is minimally present.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes a bidirectional fear-pain cycle (bio-psych) where fear amplifies central sensitization. PRT aims to break this cycle through psychological techniques, with fMRI evidence showing changes in brain activity. No social or triadic mechanisms are proposed.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper claims PRT implements the biopsychosocial model but provides minimal social content, focusing almost exclusively on biological and psychological mechanisms
conceptual_tensions_2: The term 'noziplastischer Schmerz' is central but its definition relies on exclusion of other mechanisms rather than positive criteria
additional_observations_1: The paper is a narrative review describing a specific therapy (PRT) rather than a systematic review of the BPS model
additional_observations_2: The social domain is reduced to a single mention of 'soziale Aspekte' without any specific constructs, mechanisms, or interventions
additional_observations_3: The paper uses fMRI evidence to support bio-psych integration but does not discuss social factors in the same empirical framework
synthesis_note: This paper uses the BPS label to frame PRT as an intervention that implements the model, but operationalizes it almost entirely through biological (central sensitization, neuroplasticity) and psychological (fear, catastrophizing, self-efficacy) mechanisms. The social domain is mentioned only in passing, and no triadic integration is proposed. The paper contributes a concrete example of a therapy claiming BPS grounding while being psych-dominant.
coding_rationale: Typology 'pseudo_bps' because BPS language is used but social domain is minimal and triadic integration is absent. Psych-dominant balance reflects the paper's focus on fear-avoidance and cognitive-behavioural mechanisms. Integration bio-psych is directional due to the fear-pain cycle and fMRI evidence.

title: Pain Reprocessing Therapy – Schmerz neu denken
pain_condition_detail: Chronic primary/noziplastic pain, especially chronic back pain; includes fibromyalgia, CRPS I, primary head/mouth/face pain, primary visceral pain, and primary musculoskeletal pain.
bps_function_set: background framing; conclusion; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_usage_sections: abstract; conclusion; discussion; introduction; table or figure
bps_operationalization_summary: PRT operationalizes BPS as a structured psychotherapeutic package for nociplastic pain: pain education plus mindfulness, graded exposure, cognitive restructuring, emotional processing, self-efficacy, and neuroplastic relearning. It links fear-avoidance processes to brain alarm-system mechanisms; social content is mainly outpatient implementation, work/family, and stress.
integration_mechanism_summary: Noziplastic pain is framed as a brain-generated warning signal maintained by central sensitization and fear-avoidance processes. PRT aims to calm the alarm system through education, exposure, cognitive restructuring, emotional processing, and self-efficacy. Social factors mainly enter as stress, work/family context, and outpatient implementation rather than a full social-biological pathway.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper uses BPS language while the social domain remains thin compared with nociplastic neurobiology and fear-avoidance psychology
conceptual_tensions_2: PRT claims to integrate biopsychosocial approaches but is explicitly described as strongly neurocentric
conceptual_tensions_3: The paper treats chronic primary pain as without tissue or nerve damage while also requiring careful exclusion of structural, inflammatory, infectious, tumor-related, and neuropathic causes
conceptual_tensions_4: PRT is presented as promising and guideline-concordant, but the evidence base is described as young, small, and not yet supported by systematic reviews
conceptual_tensions_5: Implementation in ambulant care is recommended, yet time, resources, therapist training, manuals, and standardized education are named as practical barriers
additional_observations_1: The first paragraph pairs pain factors as “psychosozial und somatisch”, making the article’s BPS structure a side-by-side opposition rather than a detailed mechanism
additional_observations_2: The article’s BPS use is strongest as a practical implementation rationale for PRT and weakest as a social determinants framework
additional_observations_3: Several social elements are embedded in the case example rather than developed as general social mechanisms
additional_observations_4: The paper’s main pathway is psychological reinterpretation and emotional processing changing brain-generated pain signals
additional_observations_5: The article treats diagnostic algorithms and structured instruments as ways to identify nociplastic mechanisms rather than as measures of a broad BPS model
additional_observations_6: The conclusion moves from a specific PRT intervention to a broad paradigm shift toward modern pain medicine
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mainly as a rationale for implementing PRT in chronic primary/noziplastic pain. It elaborates nociplastic neurobiology and fear-avoidance/self-efficacy processes, links them through central sensitization, neuroplasticity, and the fear-pain cycle, but social content is mostly outpatient care, work/family, stress, and implementation.
coding_rationale: BPS functions mainly as intervention rationale; bio-psych integration is mechanistic, social is thin, triadic integration partial.

title: Pain Reprocessing Therapy – Schmerz neu denken
pain_condition_detail: chronic primary pain including fibromyalgia, CRPS I, primary headache, orofacial pain, visceral pain, and musculoskeletal pain
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper operationalizes BPS through Pain Reprocessing Therapy (PRT), which integrates pain science education, cognitive restructuring, somatic tracking, and emotional processing to address noxious pain mechanisms. The model is used to explain pain as a brain-generated warning signal rather than tissue damage, with PRT providing a structured intervention to break the fear-pain-avoidance cycle.
integration_mechanism_summary: The paper proposes that noxious pain arises from central sensitization and an overactive salience network, which are maintained by fear-avoidance beliefs and misinterpreted sensory signals. PRT intervenes by educating patients about these mechanisms, restructuring maladaptive thoughts, and using somatic tracking to reclassify pain signals as harmless, thereby leveraging neuroplasticity to 'unlearn' chronic pain.
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between BPS theoretical framework and its limited social domain implementation in clinical practice
conceptual_tensions_2: Paradigm shift from biomedical to neurocentric pain understanding creates implementation challenges
conceptual_tensions_3: Terminological inconsistency between PRT and PSRT reflects ongoing conceptual development
conceptual_tensions_4: Neurocentric focus may limit applicability to patients with structural or mixed pain mechanisms
additional_observations_1: PRT represents a neurocentrically-focused implementation of BPS that emphasizes biological mechanisms (central sensitization, neuroplasticity) while treating psychological constructs as mediators of pain chronification
additional_observations_2: The paper demonstrates strong integration between biological and psychological domains through mechanistic pathways, but social factors remain peripheral despite BPS labeling
additional_observations_3: Evidence includes both clinical outcomes (pain reduction, functional improvement) and neuroimaging findings (insula and vmPFC activity changes)
additional_observations_4: Patient selection criteria are carefully defined based on noxious pain mechanisms, with clear exclusion criteria for nociceptive and neuropathic conditions
synthesis_note: This paper operationalizes the biopsychosocial model through Pain Reprocessing Therapy (PRT), demonstrating strong integration between biological (central sensitization, neuroplasticity) and psychological (fear-avoidance, cognitive restructuring) domains via mechanistic pathways. However, social factors remain minimally addressed despite BPS labeling. The paper provides evidence for PRT's effectiveness in reducing pain intensity and functional limitations, with supporting neuroimaging data showing changes in pain-related brain regions. The conceptual contribution lies in demonstrating how a neurocentric BPS implementation can achieve substantial clinical outcomes while revealing the persistent gap in social domain integration.
coding_rationale: BPS typology rated 'true_integrative' due to elaborated biological and psychological domains with mechanistic integration, though social domain remains minimal. Triadic integration scored 'none' as social factors are not meaningfully connected to the bio-psych integration. PRT's mechanistic pathway linking central sensitization, fear-avoidance beliefs, and neuroplasticity provides the core integration mechanism.

conceptual_problems_04_problem_verbatim: Obwohl die Therapieform unter einem anderen Namen geführt wird ‚Psychophysiologic Symptom Relief Therapy – PSRT‘, weist sie inhaltlich starke Überschneidungen mit der Pain Reprocessing Therapy (PRT) auf.
